frame_metadata.gps_note: First take with GPS on every frame. App frames carry a 9-key GPS block written by the F0 build; stock-camera HEICs carry Apple's full 15-key block. Both bind the frame to the Met to within a few metres.

source_note: App frames are camera-roll copies (Image Capture over USB) bound to the manifest by capture time with tools/manifest/bind-frames.py — see derived/2026-09-20-met-frames.json. App label frame (NAYH8832) is unreadable — the Mac OCR returns 'Bastern Mednerranean er Sout fudun'. Transcribed from the stock retake.

expected.title_note: The panel title. The API title for this accession is 'Glass oinochoe (perfume jug)' — a shared panel's title is not any one object's title.

expected.date_edtf_note: BCE years are astronomical: 375 BCE is -0374. Ranges are intervals; '~' marks each end when the label says 'ca.'. A named span like 'late 6th century' is written as the conventional interval and noted in date_raw.

traps.on_device_read_the_wrong_number: Candidates were ['013.1383'] — the first component lost to the frame edge (the app captures at screen aspect and cropped the card). The human corrected to 91.1.1383. The truncation warning fired; a locator should treat a warning on the accession line as 'ask', not 'offer'.
traps.tags_in_the_case: Two object tags are in frame: '91.1.1348' complete and '601' — the tail of 17.194.601 — cut by the tag's edge. A tag is a second, independent reading of the same key, and a truncated tag is a partial match, not a new number.
traps.one_of_three: The fixture's primary accession is the one the human confirmed; the panel is the unit. A pairing step that assigns this label to one work has a one-in-three chance of being right by luck.
